doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Johnny Lindsey, his father and brother Herbert
summary: Tom and Martin place Johnny Lindsey, who played bass, trombone and violin. His father played guitar and his brother Herbert played violin; Russell tried and failed to find Herbert in Chicago in 1958.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh that boy, he used to play the Trimbo Daddy.
Oh you a man, Lindsey boy? Johnny Lindsey?
Lindsey, he come there behind Buddy. Lindsey, Johnny Lindsey.

Yeah, Johnny Lindsey, he used to play bass you know. Yeah, he played bass with his daddy. Yeah, with his daddy. What does his daddy play? His daddy used to play guitar. Guitar. Yeah, and his brother used to play violin. That was Herbert Russell. Herbert.

I knew Johnny, I knew Johnny but I never knew Herbert. But Herbert was still in Chicago a few years ago and I couldn't find him. Yeah. I tried to find him in 1958, six years ago. Yeah. And he was still there. He owned him. He might be dead now but he was there. No. I told you who saw him, you remember some singers, Mack and Mack? Mack and Mack, yeah. They were still up there and they said they saw him at a grocery store every once in a while but when they tried to find him they didn't see him. I was only there a week you know and they couldn't find him that quick.
